title.narrative: CDI Curtailing Illicit Child/Women trafficking Fighting VAW, 2013-2016
CDI Curtailing Illicit Child/Women trafficking Fighting VAW, 2013-2016

description.narrative: The objective of this intervention has been "to enhance capacities of civil society to conduct advocacy to improve the well-being of children, girls and women, with special measures to strengthen rights of migrants and to act against trafficking."

Projektet är ett samarbete med lokala CSOs.It adresser illegal barn och flickor / kvinnor trafficking , vaiolence mot kvinnor ( VAW ) , flickor utbildning och arbetar för att öka kvinnors ekonomiska egenmakt ( WEE ) .Det kommer att ta itu med dessa problem genom att höja awarenessof den communityu regeringen om situationen , genom att förbättra inacting lagbestämmelser , stöd till flickor utbildning .

The project is collaboration with local CSOs.It addresses illicit child and girls/women trafficking, vaiolence against women (VAW), girls education and works to enhance women economic empowerment (WEE).It will address these problems by raising the awarenessof the communityu government about the situation, through improving the inacting of legislative provisions, support to girls education, etc.

This intervention was implemented by an Ethiopian NGO called CDI (Centre for Development Initiatives) during 2013-2016 in collaboration with 12 CBOs active in the Ethiopian regions Beshangul, Gambela and Oromia, that are all regions characterised by extreme poverty, conflict/cummunal violence and widespread harmful practices such as child marriage and FGM. An external evaluation (Case no. UF2013/75766) of this contribution identified the following results: - Changes in behavioural patterns amongst targeted groups of elderly/religious leaders, local communities and official institutions with increasing engagement to act against violence against children and women, including trafficking, and enhancing girls' participation at schools in the three regions. - Increased employment through small scale businesses for vulnerable women and IDPs, thereby strangthening their social and economic empowerment in the local communities. - Cooperatives, youth clubs, churches and mosques have become actively engaged in all three regions to act against child labour, trafficking, violence against children and women, including harmful practices such as child marriage and FGM.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
